faq.q: Why is the back of my fridge warm?
faq.a: The coils at the back are where the fridge gets rid of the heat it has taken out of the food, plus the heat from its own motor. That is why you must leave space behind it for air.
asks: Why is my fridge warm at the back?
Why are the sides of my fridge hot?

faq.q: How does a fridge keep food cold?
faq.a: A refrigerant boils in coils inside the fridge, soaking up heat. A compressor pumps it to coils outside where it releases the heat, and the cycle repeats.

faq.q: What is the humming noise from my fridge?
faq.a: The hum is the compressor, a small electric pump that squeezes the refrigerant. It switches on and off as the thermostat demands.
asks: Why does my fridge make noise?

faq.q: How does a fridge know when to switch on?
faq.a: A thermostat measures the temperature inside. When it rises above the setting, about 4 degrees for a fridge, it turns the compressor on, and off again once it is cold.
asks: What does the fridge dial do?

faq.q: Can you cool the kitchen by leaving the fridge open?
faq.a: No. The fridge dumps the heat it removes back into the same room, plus extra heat from its motor, so the kitchen actually gets slightly warmer.
asks: Does an open fridge cool a room?

facts: Food fridges are usually set to about 3 to 5 °C and freezers to about minus 18 °C.
A fridge releases more heat at its back than it removes from the food, because the compressor adds its own energy.

quiz.say: What happens to a closed kitchen if you leave the fridge door open all day?
quiz.show: What happens to a closed kitchen if you leave the fridge door open all day?
quiz.why: The fridge moves heat from the box back into the same room and adds heat from its motor, so overall the room warms a little.

wrong.1: Any cooling at the door is outweighed by the heat released at the back.
wrong.2: The motor works hard and its energy ends up as heat in the room.
